newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks expected to fall on London weakness.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks expected to fall on London weakness.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to fall on Wednesday following the weaker overnight close by local stocks listed in London and on concerns about possible government measures to rein in property prices, brokers said.

"The Hang Seng (Index) is likely to test the downside of 14,100 marks today mainly due to the fall by banks in London and continued selling on properties," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities.
The Hang Seng Index fell 87.45 points, or 0.61 percent, to close at 14,307.15 on Tuesday. The Hang Seng London Reference Index eased another 119.53 points to 14,187.62 overnight.

Banks fell across the board in London with HSBC falling about HK$4.00 to close at HK$225.20 on Tuesday. London's FTSE 100 share index posted its biggest one-day drop in 2-1/2 months to finish at 4,682.2 down 62.90 points.
"The sentiment is weak due to expectation that C.Y. Leung is going to propose new measures to curb property prices," said Peter Lai, associate director, at OCBC Securities.

Leung, the head of a post-colonial committee responsible for housing policy, is expected to submit a report outlining ideas to curb property speculation in the territory to the Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa on Wednesday.
